- spec: >
    **⚠️ THIS IS THROWAWAY CODE BY CONSTRUCTION AND TASK-423 DELETES IT.** Do not build the production subsystem here — no `UGameInstanceSubsystem`,
    no `FRunnable`, no tiering policy. Its only job is to **produce the numbers that decide whether the subsystem gets written at all.**
    Everything lives in ONE plugin-private file behind `FAutoConsoleCommandWithWorld` commands in the **`Siege.Llama.*`** namespace.
    **(1) LOAD:** `llama_model_load_from_file` on the path from `<ProjectRoot>/Models/`, `use_mmap = true` (**load-bearing for the 8 GB claim** —
    the weights are page-cache-backed, not resident), `n_ctx` 2048, small `n_ubatch`. Offload tier selectable from the command line
    (`gpulayers=-1|N|0`) so ONE build measures **full-offload / partial / CPU-only**. A load failure logs on `LogSiegeLlama` and returns —
    **never a crash, never a blocked editor.** Wrap the eval in SEH.
    **(2) PROMPT:** the three-zone layout, **verbatim shape from CONVENTIONS §8** — `ZONE A` static (system prompt, schema, place vocabulary,
    synonym table, 3 few-shots) · `ZONE B` slow (castle HP bands, mid owner, gold band) · `ZONE C` fast (roster, pending line, the utterance).
    **Fixed key order, every key always emitted (empty prints `none`), everything quantized, NO timestamps and NO coordinates.** For the spike
    the zones may be hand-written constants — but the **byte layout must match what TASK-416 will emit**, because measurement #3 is
    meaningless otherwise. Implement `llama_kv_cache_seq_rm` prefix retention and **log prefill token counts for turn 1 and turn 2 separately.**
    **(3) GRAMMAR:** a hand-written GBNF matching the plan's shape — `intent` (7 alternatives) · `kind` · `where` · `count ::= 1..30 | "all"` ·
    `when`. ⚠️ **`count` is 1–30, NOT 1–live-max — deliberately** (CONVENTIONS §1: a capped grammar would silently emit 8 for a request of 10
    and make the clarification undetectable). Use llama.cpp's C grammar/sampler API directly.
    **(4) ⚠️ THE CORPUS IS AN INPUT YOU MAY NOT AUTHOR, EDIT OR NARROW — IT IS TASK-426'S SEALED DELIVERABLE (ruling 14, CONVENTIONS §11).**
    You **write the runner, not the test set.** `Siege.Llama.SpikeEval dev=<path> holdout=<path>` **loads both CSVs BY PATH at runtime**
    (⚠️ never `#include`d — baking Siegebound sentences into the plugin would give it a Siegebound dependency it is architecturally forbidden
    to have), parses the pinned header, scores **exact-match on `{intent, kinds, counts, where}`** honouring `ExpectOutcome`
    (`Execute`/`Clarify`/`Refuse`), and prints a per-row diff table plus a score **per split, reported separately.**
    **⚠️ (4a) INTENT LIVES IN `Notes`, NOT IN A COLUMN — BUILD THE RUNNER FOR IT (CONVENTIONS §11, accepted ruling 2026-08-02).** The pinned
    header has **no `ExpectIntent` column**, but bar #5 scores intent and rows like `charge with the footmen` vs `send the footmen at their
    castle` differ in **nothing else.** TASK-426 correctly refused to add a 10th column after the seal (it would have silently broken the very
    contract you parse against) and instead prefixed every `Notes` cell. **Extract intent with `^intent=([a-z]+); `** — values are the 7
    intents plus **`none`** (Refuse rows) and **`unasserted`** (the verb itself is the ambiguity; skip the intent comparison for that row).
    **This regex is part of the pinned contract: do not reformat the `Notes` prefix, and do not "clean up" the corpus into a 10th column.**
    **⚠️ (4b) AN EMPTY CELL IS "NOT ASSERTED", NEVER "ASSERTED EMPTY".** Score it as **skipped**, not as matched — a row whose true answer is
    an empty field (`rally`, `fallback`) cannot be positively asserted in v1 and is carried in `Notes` prose. Treating empty as a pass would
    manufacture free score on exactly the rows that assert least.
    **⚠️ (4c) THE PLACE VOCABULARY IS PINNED IN CONVENTIONS §9a — use those seven spellings verbatim** in your Zone-A place list:
    `enemy_castle` · `own_castle` · `mid` · `ancient_ground_near` · `ancient_ground_far` · `nearest_mine` · `hero`. **It is `own_castle`, NOT
    `my_castle`** (the sealed `HOLD-06` asserts it, and the holdout is frozen). A spelling drift here fails the gate **for a naming reason
    rather than a model reason** — the worst way to fail it, because it reads as "the model is bad" when the model was fine.
    **YOU MAY TUNE FEW-SHOTS AGAINST `assistant_eval_dev.csv` ONLY.** ⛔ **DO NOT OPEN `assistant_eval_holdout.csv`** — TASK-413 opens it
    exactly once, and the holdout number is what is scored against the ≥ 85 % bar. **The plan's remediation ladder starts with "better
    few-shots", which IS tuning against the eval; the split is what makes that ladder honest.**
    **YOUR 3 ZONE-A FEW-SHOTS MUST BE DISJOINT FROM BOTH FILES** — no corpus sentence may appear as a few-shot. QA verifies this by literal
    string comparison at TASK-412. If you add a few-shot *because* a dev row failed, **say so in the handoff** (legitimate work; the reader
    must know the coverage was reactive).
    ⚠️ **MULTI-KIND IS IN SCOPE (ruling 15):** the schema carries index-aligned `Kinds`/`Counts` with a hard cap of 3, so the GBNF in (3) emits
    a **selection list of 1..3 `{kind, count}` pairs** — the cap lives in the grammar, not only in the parser.
    **(5) INSTRUMENTATION — the numbers ARE the deliverable.** Emit, machine-readable and grep-able: per-frame delta-time samples around
    prefill/decode with a **hitch histogram reporting WORST and p99, never mean**; TTFT; wall-clock for ~60 constrained tokens; turn-1 vs
    turn-2 prefill token counts; peak VRAM (via the backend) and process RSS. Command `Siege.Llama.SpikeBench tier=<...> iters=<N>`.
    **NO game-lane code, NO Siegebound types, NO `Content/` changes, NO Git.** The plugin must keep knowing nothing about Siegebound —
    the spike's snapshot text is a hard-coded constant, not a `Capture()` call.

#### TASK-411 — [LLM-1b] SPIKE MEASUREMENT #6 — does a focused `UEditableTextBox` starve Enhanced Input of WASD? (gameplay-programmer)
- assignee: gameplay-programmer
- status: **qa-passed** — 🔍 **FULL QA REVIEW COMPLETE 2026-08-02 (`qa/TASK-411.md`): PASS, 0 BLOCKER · 6 WARN · 6 NIT.** First full review of this task (TASK-412 was targeted-confirmation only and scoped itself out). **All six root-cause citations re-derived from installed UE 5.8 source, not relayed** — `SlateApplication.cpp:5018`/`:5069` · `MainFrameActions.cpp:97/275/283` · `DebuggerCommands.cpp:358` · `SlateEditableTextLayout.cpp:1448` · `SceneViewport.cpp:1288` · `PlayerController.cpp:6313`/`:6446`. **TASK-413's "passes 2 and 3 would have survived" is REFUTED** — a plain box does not absorb Escape, so Escape ends PIE from any pass; the frame-0 diagnosis is superseded. All three fixes gated: the box-exclusion `return false` at `cpp:582` sits before the ancestor walk and is unbypassable, so a harness fault cannot be mislabelled as "the hero didn't move" **or vice versa**; **no path turns a suppressed observation into a measured negative** (`DescribeObservation` is the only printer and branches on `!bInjected` first); retries return **before** `GetResults().Add`, so `GetResults()[0]` is always the CONTROL row and exhaustion ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE, never a default. **No false-PASS path constructible.** Bank-as-you-go + PARTIAL banner verified; `focus-at-press` sampled pre-injection; comment trap re-run on RAW reads (zero unterminated, zero premature `*/`); `Walker` alive in **both** focus helpers; M8 declaration verbatim; every signature/include checked against 5.8. ⚖️ **OPEN-CAVEAT RULING: the `MODE A Enter → YES` hypothesis is SOUND and FORCED by `SlateEditableTextLayout.cpp:1092` — Enter NEVER reaches the game from a focused box in EITHER input mode, so TASK-424 must NOT price Enter as an input-mode cost; the RMB half of the A/B result is the real fallback cost, the Enter half is confounded.** ⚠️ **Two run-time confounds the runner must control, neither able to flip the binary: RMB depends on an unguarded OS cursor position (park it over the viewport and check the printed `RMB cursor was at (x, y)`), and a stray human W/A/S/D forces FAIL — the EXPENSIVE direction, flipping the design to `UIOnly`. Prefer the inline `BANKED row N/3` lines over `Siege.Assistant.InputProbeReport`, which carries no run identity after an aborted arm.** **Bar #6 is DE-PROVISIONALISED on the QA side.** ⚙️ **Rework record (2026-08-02, post-TASK-413): THE PROBE COULD NOT EARN AN ANSWER, AND ONE ROOT CAUSE EXPLAINS BOTH FAILURES.** `handoffs/TASK-411-programmer.md` §"Rework". Prior state (✅ RESOLVED — BUILDS GREEN, TASK-409's fourth pass: C4458 shadow fix + TASK-417's `"SlateCore"`, `Result: Succeeded`, zero diagnostics) still holds; the C4458 `Walker` rename is intact. **NOT COMPILED — quiet-module law (a build-master is mid model fetch).**
- 🎯 **ROOT CAUSE OF TASK-413 BAR #6 — the CONTROL pass called `FSlateApplication::ClearKeyboardFocus()`:** >
    `FSlateApplication::ProcessKeyDownEvent` routes a key event **ONLY along `SlateUser->GetFocusPath()`** (`SlateApplication.cpp:5018`).
    With focus cleared that path is **EMPTY**, so **(a)** the synthetic W/A/S/D reached no widget, never `SViewport`, so
    `UGameViewportClient::InputKey` was never called and `UPlayerInput` never saw them ⇒ the standalone `-game` **CONTROL-FAILED, PATH 0.00**;
    and **(b)** the event fell through to `UnhandledKeyDownEventHandler` (`:5069`) → `FMainFrameActionCallbacks::OnUnhandledKeyDownEvent`
    (`MainFrameActions.cpp:275`) → `FPlayWorldCommands::GlobalPlayWorldActions`, where **`StopPlaySession` is bound to the Escape chord**
    (`DebuggerCommands.cpp:358`) ⇒ **PIE ended at the end of pass 1.** ⚠️ **The `-ExecCmds`-frame-0 diagnosis was NOT the cause** — it is a
    real hazard (now gated) but it cannot explain a CONTROL that ran seconds after frame 0. All five citations read from UE 5.8 engine source.
    ⚠️ **Escape ends PIE in EVERY pass, focused or not** — a plain `UEditableTextBox` does **not** absorb it (`HandleEscape()` returns false
    with `RevertTextOnEscape=false`, `SlateEditableTextLayout.cpp:1102`/`:1448`) and `FSceneViewport::OnKeyDown` returns **Unhandled** when the
    viewport client does not consume the key (`SceneViewport.cpp:1288`). Build-master's "passes 2 and 3 would have survived" does not hold.
- 🔧 **THE THREE FIXES (`SiegeAssistantInputProbe.{h,cpp}` only — no other file touched):** >
    **(1)** CONTROL now focuses the **game viewport widget** (the real shipping focus target; **not** implied by the input mode —
    `FInputModeDataBase::SetFocusAndLocking` focuses only a *valid* `WidgetToFocus`, `PlayerController.cpp:6313`), re-asserts it every arming
    frame and **verifies** it before typing; a control that never had it is stamped a **HARNESS fault** in those words, not "the hero did not move".
    **(2)** Escape is **NOT INJECTED in a PIE world** (policy `Auto`; `escape` forces it, `noescape` bans it). A suppressed observation reports
    **NOT INJECTED**, never "swallowed". The Escape matrix is a standalone `-game` measurement.
    **(3)** The command **ARMS**, it does not start: an `FTSTicker` waits for controller + possessed pawn + `UPlayerInput` + game viewport widget
    **and** a consecutive-warm-frame window (defaults 5 s / 45 frames ≤ 50 ms, budget 120 s) — this is the `~3 FPS for ~25 s` L_Arena guard.
    **CONTROL is itself the readiness test and is retried up to 4× with every failed attempt printed.** Rows are **banked + logged one at a time**,
    and a partial run prints a loud **PARTIAL** banner instead of "No probe has run". New: `Siege.Assistant.InputProbeCancel`.
    ✅ **Every refusal guard preserved** (failed control ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE never PASS · lost focus ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE · text did not land ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE),
    and the one result TASK-413 did establish (**MODE B UIOnly swallows RMB + Enter; MODE A GameAndUI fires both**) is still measured and reported,
    now with focus-at-press recorded per observation so a contaminated row is visible rather than silently wrong.

    a Defender firewall prompt on first launch of a shipped game is unacceptable). **Do NOT add the `SiegeLlama` plugin dependency here** —
    the game lane does not call the subsystem until Wave 1's B2.
    **(1) `SiegeAssistantCommand.h` = THE PURE-DATA HEADER** (the `UnitCommand.h` / `TeamId.h` precedent): `ESiegeAssistantIntent`,
    `FSiegeAssistantCommand` (**`uint8`/`int32`/`FName` ONLY** — so M8 P2 takes it over the wire as-is, ~30 bytes at the cap, with inference
    staying client-local), `static constexpr int32 SiegeAssistantMaxSelectionKinds = 3`, the free function `ParseSiegeAssistantCommand`, and
    **`DECLARE_LOG_CATEGORY_EXTERN(LogSiegeAssistant, Log, All)`**.
    ⚠️ **THE SELECTION IS MULTI-KIND (manager ruling 15 — my first pin was WRONG and is corrected).** `TArray<FName> Kinds` +
    `TArray<int32> Counts`, **index-aligned parallel arrays, NEVER an array of structs** (that is what keeps the type to `FName`/`int32` only
    and preserves the P2 "takes it as-is" property). Hard cap `SiegeAssistantMaxSelectionKinds`. Without this the feature's own flagship
    sentence — *"send 10 footmen **with a sorcerer** to the nearest ancient ground"* — is inexpressible.
    This header is what TASK-416 includes — **its contents are pinned; changing a name breaks the link and is an automatic QA FAIL.**
    **(2) `USiegeAssistantGrammar::Build(const TArray<FName>& UnitKinds, const TArray<FName>& PlaceNames)` — PURE AND DETERMINISTIC.**
    **No `UWorld`, no engine state, no UObject inputs — this shape is deliberate**: it decouples A4 from A3 entirely and is what makes the
    automation tests genuinely cheap, with no model in the loop. Emits the plan's GBNF: `intent` (the 7 enum values, derived from
    `ESiegeAssistantIntent` so there is ONE source) · `kind` and `where` **GENERATED from the passed arrays** (a small model physically cannot
    name a unit that does not exist — grounding moves out of the weights and into the grammar) · **`count ::= 1..30 | "all"`** ·
    `when ::= "now" | { kind, at_least }` · and a **`selection` list of 1..`SiegeAssistantMaxSelectionKinds` `{kind, count}` pairs**.
    ⚠️ **THE CAP LIVES IN THE GRAMMAR, NOT ONLY IN THE PARSER** — an unbounded repetition rule is precisely what a small model rambles into,
    and a bounded alternation costs nothing. The parser then enforces `Kinds.Num() == Counts.Num()`; **a mismatch is a parse FAILURE, never a
    silent truncation.**
    ⚠️ **`count` IS 1–30, NOT 1–LIVE-MAX, DELIBERATELY** — a grammar capped at the live 8 would make a request for 10 silently emit 8, i.e. the
    exact valid-shaped-wrong-command failure this whole design exists to prevent, with the clarification made **undetectable** (CONVENTIONS §1).
    A later "optimization" tightening this range is introducing the defect.
    **(3) `ParseSiegeAssistantCommand`** — strict: reject unknown keys, reject out-of-range counts, map `"all"` → `Count = 0`, `"now"` →
    `TriggerKind = NAME_None`. **Never partially fills on failure**; returns a reason string. **No player-facing text is produced here** —
    reason codes only (§3).
    **(4) `USiegeAssistantVocabulary : UDataAsset`** with `UnitSynonyms` / `PlaceSynonyms` / `IntentSynonyms` (`FSiegeAssistantSynonym`) and
    `BuildSynonymTable()` emitting the **Zone-A** synonym block with **deterministic ordering** (Zone A must be byte-stable).
    ⚠️ **The vocabulary feeds the PROMPT, never the grammar** — the grammar emits canonical symbols only. ⚠️ **It must disambiguate
    Sorcerer vs Wizard, which are different cards.** The class ships with sane C++ defaults so the game works before the asset exists; the
    **asset instance is TASK-421's** deliverable.
    **(5) AUTOMATION TESTS — the one place unit tests are genuinely cheap here.** `IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST` under
    `#if WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS` (no new module needed — `AutomationTest.h` is in `Core`). Cover at minimum: determinism (same inputs ⇒
    byte-identical GBNF, run twice) · empty roster (grammar still well-formed, `kind` degenerate case handled) · the full 7-intent alternation ·
    **`count` upper bound is exactly 30** · a place list with one entry · round-trip `Build` → a hand-written conforming JSON →
    `ParseSiegeAssistantCommand` → the expected struct · and **at least 3 malformed JSONs that MUST be rejected**.
    **MULTI-KIND CASES ARE MANDATORY:** a 1-kind selection · a 2-kind selection (the flagship *"10 footmen with a sorcerer"*) · a 3-kind
    selection at the cap · **a 4-kind attempt that the GRAMMAR must not admit** · and **a `Kinds`/`Counts` length mismatch that the PARSER
    must reject rather than truncate.**
    **NO snapshot code, NO subsystem code, NO `Content/` asset, NO Git, NO compile.**

    ley-warden empowerer; the Wizard is the AoE fireball caster. A shared alias makes the assistant confidently command the wrong unit, which
    is exactly the valid-shaped-wrong-command failure the whole design exists to prevent. **No alias may appear in two rows** — check it.

    `ancient_ground_far` (`the far ancient ground`, `their ancient ground`) · **`nearest_mine`** (`the nearest mine`, `the mine`) · `hero`.

### ⛔ PROVENANCE — READ FIRST

> ⛔ **§12f RESERVED RUNG 3 TO JONATHAN BY NAME. FLAG (g) OF THE LLM-ASSISTANT BATCH AND THE TASK-428 SPEC BOTH FORBID AN AGENT PROPOSING IT. ⇒ ✅ HE EXERCISED IT HIMSELF. THE RESERVATION WAS HONOURED, NOT BYPASSED.**

⚖️ **Both sentences stay true and both stay on the record:** *no agent may propose this rung* — unchanged, still binding for the next one — and *Jonathan opened this one*. ⛔ **No future agent may cite this batch as precedent for proposing a rung.** The precedent set here is about **how a rung is executed once opened**, never about who may open it.

### ⭐ THE OUTCOME LAW — WRITTEN BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT RUNS, NOT AFTER

> ⭐ **A BATCH THAT ENDS AT STOP 1, HAVING FIXED THE WIRE FORMAT AND SAVED WEEKS, IS THE BEST RESULT AVAILABLE AND IS REPORTED AS A SUCCESS.**

⛔ **No handoff, QA report, board entry or Slack post may frame an early stop as a failure, a cancellation, or *"the fine-tune didn't happen"*.** Fixing D1 is **hours**; QLoRA is **weeks**. ⚖️ **The reason this is dated before the run is that an early stop is only credible as a success if it was declared one in advance** — declared afterwards it reads as consolation, which is how a pipeline learns to push past its own stops. ⚠️ **And the symmetric trap is named too: this is NOT a licence to stop early to avoid hard work.** *"It felt like the wire format was the problem"* is not STOP 1 — **a stop is a number, in writing, against a rule written before the run**, and its denominator is M0's measured noise floor.

### ⛔ THE THREE DIVERGENCES (D1 / D2 / D3) — the whole reason this batch is measurement-first

| # | Divergence | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **Chat template.** Harness wraps in Qwen3's template (Zone A `system`, B+C `user`, `add_generation_prompt=true`); `USiegeAssistantComponent::ComposeTurnPrompt` **concatenates raw, no roles.** | ⛔ **Every number on record — 18 → 19 → 20, the 66.7 % — describes a prompt shape the game never produces.** Qwen3 is post-trained on its template ⇒ raw concat is off-distribution **by construction.** |
| **D2** | **Roster collapse.** Shipped Zone C caps at `MaxRosterKinds = 8` and collapses the tail; the harness prints all **13**, on `t0`. | ⛔ **`holdout2` may be authored against a board the game does not render**, inside the block the model reads unit names from. |
| **D3** | **Sparse boards unmeasurable.** `VerifyFixtureKindParity` demands every fixture carry all 13 kinds; the GBNF is built from `SpikeRoster`, not the fixture. | The few-shots-name-a-kind-the-board-lacks seam **cannot be measured by the only instrument that exists.** |

⚖️ **This is §12a's two-lane hole (`DA_AssistantVocabulary`) recurring THREE more times — same shape, different seam: the lanes agree on everything a reader can check and differ in content the reader never sees.** Each was found by reading **the shipped path** rather than the measured one.

### 🔒 THE TWO PRE-REGISTERED STOPS + THE THREE DECISION RULES

- ⛔ **STOP 1 — WIRE FORMAT.** `chat=0` materially below `chat=1` ⇒ **fix the runtime wire format, re-measure, re-ask. TRAINING IS NOT AUTHORISED until the shipped lane has been measured at its own best.**
- ⛔ **STOP 2 — ROSTER SEAM.** M3's diff fails on the roster block ⇒ **resolve D2 first.**
- **M2 ≈ M1 within M0's band** ⇒ gap is **capability**; mix is class-driven from M5.
- **M2 materially worse than M1** ⇒ gap is **distribution**; mix is voice-heavy; fine-tuning very likely works.
- ⛔ **M2 already ≥ 13/15-equivalent on the shipped shape** ⇒ **DO NOT TRAIN.** Re-run the gate arithmetic — the feature may already pass once the wire format is honest.
- ⚠️ **"MATERIALLY" IS DEFINED BY M0, NOT BY JUDGEMENT.** ⛔ **A stop evaluated before M0 has printed a number has no denominator.**

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim:** *"we need a way to be able to close the AI chat window in the game. Lets make it to where if you press "enter" without anything typed in the box then it will close. After that I will resume testing"*.

**Law was written FIRST (house rule):** CONVENTIONS "In-match LLM command assistant" **`AS-§6` RULING A-2 — THE CONSOLE'S CLOSE ROUTES** (the four routes enumerated, the close-is-not-a-cancel rule restated, the ordering hazard named, and Escape left OPEN as Jonathan's).

### ⚖️ THE FOUR MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — THE CHANGE LANDS IN `HandleTextCommitted`, NOT IN `SubmitPressed`. This is the whole design decision and it is one symbol wide.**
`HandleTextCommitted` **already** filters to `ETextCommit::OnEnter` only — it exists because `OnUserMovedFocus` and `OnCleared` arrive at the same delegate and *"treating either as an order would let a click elsewhere submit a half-typed sentence."* ⇒ **That filter is exactly Jonathan's trigger: an `Enter` keypress, and nothing else.** ⛔ **`SubmitPressed` is `BlueprintCallable`, reachable from routes that are not the key, and its empty-string branch is a DIFFERENT, ratified protection (no model call on a blank prompt — queue depth is 1). Moving the close there would make "some other caller passed an empty string" mean "close the window", which nobody asked for.**

**RULING 2 — ⚠️ THE ORDERING QUESTION IS UNMEASURED, SO THE FIX IS BUILT TO BE CORRECT IN *BOTH* WORLDS RATHER THAN TO BET ON ONE.**
⛔ `Enter` would now do **three jobs**: open the console (TASK-445's `IA_AssistantConsole`) · submit a typed line · close it when empty. **World A — Slate consumes the key while the input box has focus** (TASK-445's reasoning, ⚠️ *"reasoning, not measurement"*): Enhanced Input never sees it, the controller toggle never fires while open, the three jobs never collide, and route 4 is the ONLY thing that can close the box. **World B — Enhanced Input sees it too:** an empty-box press would `CloseConsole()` → broadcast → the controller clears the posture → `OnAssistantConsolePressed` then finds the console CLOSED and takes the **open** branch ⇒ **close-then-reopen, which reads to the player as "the close key does nothing."**
⭐ **AND JONATHAN'S OWN REPORT IS EVIDENCE FOR WORLD A, WHICH IS WHY THIS FIX IS THE RIGHT ONE:** the controller's toggle already closes the console (`SiegePlayerController.cpp:4270`, close-first and un-gated). **If Enhanced Input were receiving `Enter` while the box had focus, the console would ALREADY close on `Enter` — and his complaint is that it does not.** ⚖️ **That is corroboration, not a measurement, and it is recorded as corroboration.**
⇒ **TASK-505 ships a re-open suppression window and states which world it relied on.** ✅ **The suppression is SAFE ALREADY: `OnAssistantConsolePressed` re-reads `IsConsoleOpen()` after `OpenConsole()` and releases the posture on a refusal (`:4365`) — so a refused re-open cannot strand the cursor in `GameAndUI`.**

**RULING 3 — ⛔ THE FIX IS COMPILED NOW AND COMMITTED LATER, WITH TASK-481. THE COMPILE AND THE COMMIT ARE SPLIT ON PURPOSE.**
TASK-481 is **PARTIAL**: Stage A compiled clean and its **source is deliberately UNCOMMITTED** because `FT-§16`'s dev-split proof could not run (no editor, no MCP). ⚖️ **I rule the fold IN for the compile and the commit, and OUT for the measurement:**
- ✅ **FOLD THE SOURCE.** The console widget is **not on the dev-split's path** — a different TU, zero call sites from `SpikeEval`, no shared symbol. Adding it cannot move a score that grades JSON emitted by the spike. **One compile, one commit, one gate — Jonathan does not pay for a second cycle.**
- ⛔ **DO NOT FOLD THE MEASUREMENT INTO HIS PLAYTEST.** The §16 proof needs an exclusive editor + PIE + **the whole GPU** (`SC-§16`: two model-load paths WON'T FIT ⇒ one lane per session), and **Jonathan is at the keyboard and wants to play.** ⇒ **TASK-507 is COMPILE-ONLY: no MCP, no PIE, no `SpikeEval`, no Git.** The measurement and the single combined commit stay exactly where they are, in TASK-481, and run when he hands the machine over.
- ⚠️ **THE COST OF THIS RULING, STATED: Stage-A source AND the console fix both sit UNCOMMITTED through his playtest.** That is already the state Stage A is in; the fix adds one more uncommitted file to the same pending commit. **`main` stays 29 ahead and nothing is pushed.**
- ⛔ **IF TASK-505 FAILS TO COMPILE, THE CONSOLE FIX IS THE THING THAT STOPS — NEVER STAGE A.** Build-master reports the errors and hands back to the programmer; **it does not `git checkout`/revert an uncommitted file** (that would destroy work that has no commit to fall back to).

**RULING 4 — 🧑 THE ESCAPE QUESTION GOES TO JONATHAN AS A QUESTION, AND IT DOES NOT BLOCK HIS FIX.**
⚠️ **This is the SECOND time the same underlying need has surfaced** — flagged item (t) recorded that **Escape does not close the console** (TASK-444 left it unabsorbed on purpose so the shipped cancel routes keep firing), and now he has hit the missing close in play. ⇒ **The conventional answer is Escape, and it needs no key overloading at all** — but **§2 says the assistant may never degrade a shipped key**, and Escape already means *"cancel"* in placement, targeting and group-pick. ⛔ **I am not deciding it.** It rides TASK-508 as a one-line question at the playtest he is already doing. **His answer gets written into `AS-§6 A-2`, not into a code comment.**

**Design authority = the approved plan `C:\Users\wesel\.claude\plans\ok-there-are-a-cheerful-mccarthy.md`** — plan mode, **every engine claim verified first-hand against installed UE 5.8 source at `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source` and against the `Saved/Logs/` sessions**, ExitPlanMode-approved. ⛔ **The plan file wins over any board summary. The architecture is NOT re-litigated.**

📌 **A FINDING RECORDED AT AUTHORING, BECAUSE IT WILL MISLEAD SOMEBODY: `ok-there-are-a-cheerful-mccarthy.md` IS THE SAME PLAN PATH `KBD-§`'s LAW CITES.** The plan-file slot was **OVERWRITTEN** — the file on disk today is **this** feature's plan; the keyboard-layout plan is **gone**. ⛔ **A reader following `KBD-§1`'s citation lands here.** `KBD`'s law is complete in `KBD-§0..§11` and needs no plan re-read; ⛔ **nobody "reconciles" the two by editing the wrong section.**

### ⭐ THE DIAGNOSIS IN ONE SCREEN — ⛔ IT IS NOT A MISSING PATH CALCULATOR

**Movement is ALREADY real pathfinding** — `MoveToActor`/`MoveToLocation` with `bUsePathfinding=true`, at **four sites only** (`SummonedUnit.cpp:2446` · `:2473` · `:2479` · `:2585`, plus `MinerUnit.cpp:867`/`:932`). ⛔ **Jonathan's *"it may have to be some sort of path calculator but I'm not sure"* is ANSWERED by that line, not obeyed literally.** Two real causes, both cited:

- **⭐ CAUSE 1 — the navmesh rebuilds ONE TILE AT A TIME, ~216 s per match.** `DefaultEngine.ini:294`'s `bDoFullyAsyncNavDataGathering=True` costs a hard serialization: `RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5892-5896` submits **`NumTasksToSubmit = 1`** when gathering is off the game thread. **738 blocking HISM instances dirty essentially the whole 28×13 = 364-column grid; MEASURED 326 tiles / ~216 s / ~1.5 tiles/s** (`handoffs/TASK-366-buildmaster.md:143-152`), corroborated by an independent **178 s** figure (`handoffs/TASK-350-buildmaster.md:19`). **Tiles sort by seed location and `GetSeedLocations` collects PLAYER-PAWN POSITIONS ONLY (`:7047-7059`)** ⇒ **the far field settles LAST**, and a unit ordered across the map walks over tiles still holding the **pre-scatter bake**: the navmesh says open ground, the rock's collider says no.
- **⭐ CAUSE 2 — nothing detects a stuck unit.** `UPathFollowingComponent` already declares **`EPathFollowingResult::Blocked` after <10 uu in 5.0 s** (`PathFollowingComponent.cpp:136-144`) — but **there is NO `OnMoveCompleted` override anywhere in the project and ZERO `EPathFollowingResult` references**, so the verdict is discarded and 0.25 s later `SummonedUnit.cpp:2440` re-issues the **byte-identical** request. **A silent 5-second livelock, with no telemetry** (the `Failed` log at `:2485` is gated on `bGoalChanged`).
- **CAUSE 3 — the traversability guarantee is dishonest AND holds a determinism hole.** `Traversability CONFIRMED` fires at **+5.03 s** against a ~3 %-built navmesh (`BattlefieldScatter.cpp:1953` reads `IsNavigationBeingBuilt` idle ~211 s early), and the cull-retry path (`:2044-2049`) **DELETES INSTANCES** on that timing-dependent answer ⇒ **the shipped instance set is not a pure function of the seed** (`TASKBOARD.md:11044`).

### ⛔ THREE THEORIES RULED OUT — RECORDED SO THEY CANNOT BE RE-PROPOSED (`NAV-§2` carries the full evidence)

| ❌ theory | why it is dead |
|---|---|
| **raise `AgentRadius`** | `walkableRadius = CeilToInt(AgentRadius / CellSize)` (`RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5306`); at `CellSize=32`, `ceil(34/32)=2` voxels = **64 uu real clearance**, already covering every capsule (30/40/45/**60** Ogre). ⭐ **Any value in (32, 64] yields a BYTE-IDENTICAL navmesh.** 65+ **loses** walkable area, inflates the gather box, and fails nav registration (`FNavAgentProperties::IsEquivalent`, `Precision=5.f`). The engine forbids the actor-side route outright (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:4246`). |
| **re-save `L_Arena`'s bake** | The `Serialize … loaded empty` warnings fire at `00.44.33:603`, **inside the `LoadMap: /Game/Maps/L_MainMenu` window** (log `:1747`). **`L_Arena` loads at `:1847` with NO warning.** The stale bake is the **MENU map's**. ⇒ ⛔ **NO `L_Arena` save, NO new Jonathan exception — the spent one (`TASKBOARD.md:9485-9489`, *"do not cite it twice"*) stays spent.** |
| **crowd / RVO avoidance** | `UCrowdFollowingComponent` is a **permanent** per-agent per-frame solve at 60–120 units with **no FPS baseline** to measure it — against Jonathan's own *"without it being too costly to compute."* ⛔ **And `bUseRVOAvoidance` avoids *pawns*, not static geometry: rocks are `ECC_WorldStatic` HISM colliders, invisible to it. It would not move a unit around a rock at any radius.** |

### ⚖️ THE NINE MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — ⛔ THE SCALE BASELINE IS SETTLED. ⛔ NO AGENT RE-OPENS IT.**
The castle **already went 3× per dimension once** (CASTLE-3X, TASK-347..351, shipped 2026-07-29 at `2437.9 × 2461.5 × 2694.2 uu`, 28,702 tris, hollow). Jonathan was asked which baseline he meant, was shown that *"another 3× from today"* means **729× the ORIGINAL blockout's volume** together with its consequences, and **chose it deliberately.** ⇒ **Target `7326 × 7380 × 8082 uu` ±10 %** (`WR-§0`; 3× the as-shipped mesh is `7313.7 × 7384.5 × 8082.6`, inside the same band — **both numbers recorded so neither reads as a contradiction**). ⛔ **A task that asks "did he mean the original?" has not read this line.**

**RULING 2 — ⭐⛔ THE SHELL SCALES; THE STEP CHAIN DOES NOT. THIS IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED AN UNENTERABLE CASTLE.**
A naive uniform ×3 takes the threshold chain `0→20→58` (**max step 38 uu**) to `0→60→174` (**max step 114 uu**) — ⛔ **far past Recast's agent step AND `AHeroCharacter::HeroMaxStepHeight` (50)** ⇒ ⛔⛔ **nothing enters the castle: the hollow interior, the team-gated entry (TASK-349's loop-4 B4 fix) and interior spawning all die silently, and the mesh readback would still PASS every bounds check.** ⇒ **`WR-§1` makes the re-derived approach (≤40 uu treads, or a ≤30° ramp, reaching floor `z ≈ 174`) the art task's NAMED, MEASURED deliverable.** ⚖️ **The general form is now law: `SC-§34`'s human-scale exemption — *a castle 3× taller does not get 3× the step height; the units did not grow.***

**RULING 3 — ⭐⭐ CLICK → SYMBOL, ⛔ NEVER CLICK → COORDINATE. THE WHOLE FEATURE SPENDS ZERO PROMPT CHARACTERS.**
- ⛔ **An arbitrary click on a battlefield map is a CONTINUOUS WORLD COORDINATE, and the shipped vocabulary has NO PRIMITIVE FOR ONE** (`SiegeAssistantCommand.h:117-120` — *"every field is a SYMBOL, never a coordinate"*). ⚠️ **AS-§21 shipped `{"in":"<place>"}` for exactly THREE region-bearing places and DELIBERATELY REFUSED to invent a radius for the other four.**
- ✅ **THE RULING: only the seven `PlaceVocabulary` markers are HIT-TESTABLE, drawn at their `ResolvePlace` positions; a click inserts the LITERAL SYMBOL (`ancient_ground_near`) into the shipped console's input box; a click on empty map does NOTHING.** ⭐ **A marker's hit box is a WIDGET RECT, not a world radius — so no number describing world space is invented and `AS-§21.4` is honoured exactly rather than argued around.**
- ⇒ ⭐ **`ZoneA` STAYS BYTE-FROZEN AT `5658` AND TASK-564 ASSERTS IT.** ⛔ **Assert in chars/bytes; ⛔ NO token figure may be quoted or derived anywhere in this batch (`AS-§12g`; the shipped `zoneA_tok` has still never been printed — TASK-552 owes it).**
- ⛔ **NO new place symbol, grid cell, snap radius, coordinate field or eighth `who` shape.** Each is a new spatial primitive needing **a number Jonathan supplies.** ⚠️ **Whether the decorative `SM_POI_01..04` props should become nameable places is FLAGGED (D8), ⛔ not assumed.**

**RULING 4 — ⭐ THE MAP IS PAINTED IN C++, NOT ASSEMBLED IN UMG. THIS COLLAPSES THE BATCH'S MOST DANGEROUS TASK.**
Markers and dots are drawn in **`NativeOnPaint` / `FSlateDrawElement`**, ⛔ **never as UMG child widgets.** ⚖️ **It dodges the MCP widget-tree authoring limit AND the duplicate-and-reparent runtime-repaint corruption class (≈9 wasted fixes on this project) in one stroke, and it makes marker geometry a SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH shared by the painter and by `NativeOnMouseButtonDown` — so what you can see and what you can click can never disagree.** ⇒ **`WBP_WarMap` supplies ONLY a background panel, a reveal button, a close button and a status line, and is BUILT FRESH** (`WBP_SessionMenu` is the standing proof that is achievable).

**RULING 5 — ⛔ THE NPC IS AN AVATAR. ⛔ THE CONSOLE IS NOT GATED.**
One `USiegeAssistantComponent`, one prompt, one model, one console widget. ⛔ **No second LLM path, no NPC-specific prompt zone, no parallel conversation state.** ⛔⛔ **NO TASK MAY ADD A PROXIMITY CONDITION TO THE EXISTING CONSOLE OPEN PATH** — Jonathan said in terms *"the console still works anywhere."* ⚖️ **Stated this hard because *"the NPC is the avatar for the AI"* is one small step from *"the AI needs the NPC"*, and that step deletes a shipped feature.**

**RULING 6 — ⛔ THE 30-GOLD REVEAL IS AN ECONOMY CHANGE, AND *"THE AI NEVER SPENDS GOLD"* SURVIVES IT INTACT.**
The spend is initiated by **the player's own click**, executed on the **authority** via the shipped `ASiegePlayerState::SpendGold`, and is ⛔ **unreachable from every assistant command path.** ✅ **QA CRITERION: grep the assistant executor for any reveal/gold call and report ZERO.** ⚖️ **Written into law (`WR-§7`) because it will look like a violation to someone reading fast, and because the fix for a misread would be to route it through the assistant — which is the actual violation.** **Default: FROZEN SNAPSHOT at purchase, cleared on close** — his own *"pay another 30 gold to reveal the NEW locations"* presupposes staleness. ⚠️ **HONEST LIMITATION RECORDED: on a listen server the client already holds the enemy actors (Tier B), so this is an ECONOMY/UI gate, ⛔ not an anti-cheat boundary.**

**RULING 7 — ⛔ THE TORCHES AND THE NPC ARE SPAWNED BY `ACastle`, ⛔ NEVER PLACED IN `L_Arena`.**
⚖️ **Three load-bearing reasons: (1) `L_Arena` is the asset this project is under standing orders never to save; (2) both castles get identical furnishing BY CONSTRUCTION with no mirror step to get wrong; (3) the anchors move with the castle actor forever.** ⛔ **Lights are MOVABLE with `CastShadows = false`** — not a preference: **a runtime-spawned light CANNOT use a baked static shadow map**, and the only Static path needs a lighting build **plus an `L_Arena` save**. ⚠️ **NO FPS BASELINE EXISTS** (M7's TASK-183 never ran) ⇒ **the perf verdict is Jonathan's eye; ⛔ no agent reports a frame-rate claim.**

### ⚖️ THE FOUR RULINGS FOR THIS WAVE (full reasoning in `WM-§1..§6` — cited, not restated)

1. **ELEVATION = RUNTIME ONE-TIME TRACE BAKE PER MATCH (`WM-§2`).** Hills re-roll per match seed (verified at source) ⇒ an offline bake lies and a ground-only bake is uniform gray. 7,800 traces once per match, lazy on first open, clamp-normalized so castles don't erase hills. ⛔ No offline asset, no per-frame cost.
2. **POI ICONS ARE DISPLAY-ONLY; `WR-§6`'s CLICK→SYMBOL LAW IS UNTOUCHED (`WM-§1`).** Positions from world actors (`AGoldNode` · `AAncientGround` · `ACastle` — the ally-dot precedent), ⛔ never from a new symbol, grid or coordinate. ⚖️ **D8 stays OPEN — icons ≠ nameable AI places; his ask adds VISUALS, not vocabulary.** `ADeepMine` is NOT a POI (default, flagged).
3. **BLUE DOTS = THE SHIPPED ALLY-DOT LAYER, VERIFIED + MADE LEGIBLE, NOT RE-AUTHORED (`WM-§3`).** Enemy dots stay behind the 30-gold reveal (`WR-§7` stands; own units only, per his words).
4. **TASK-580 (the real snapshot seed) IS UN-HELD — FINALIZED 2026-08-29 on VID-003 (`WM-§5` dated block):** the pristine first-open was NOT cleanly captured (mid-session clip; only with-snapshot strings observed) ⇒ TASK-579's instrument is **RETIRED-AS-MOOT, not observed-passed** — this wave makes markers-on-open the new normal, so the pair is unrepeatable, and Jonathan's verbatim directive supersedes the interim measure. 580 folds into this wave under its own ID. ⛔⛔ **BUT the clip shows markers=0 WITH the with-snapshot branch live (`WarMapWidget.cpp:871-873`'s documented case) ⇒ 580 is `blocked-by` TASK-691 (diagnose-first) — a seed aimed before that ruling might land an equally marker-less snapshot and fix nothing.** ⛔ **The 571 CONSOLE half (TASK-552's sentences + numbers) stays owed separately and is NOT discharged by anything here.**

### 🙋 FOR JONATHAN — proceeding defaults (answer only if you disagree; nothing waits on these)

|---|---|---|
| J1 | Elevation-bake scope | Runtime one-time trace capture per match (hills move per seed — an offline bake would show hills where they aren't). Cost: 7,800 traces ONCE on first map open, zero per-frame. |
| J2 | Icon style | Flat white glyphs (pickaxe/nugget · rune ring · keep silhouette), tinted in code — castles blue/red via the team palette, mines/ancient grounds neutral. Restyle later is cheap (swap 3 textures, no code). |

## MARKS + RECALL + GHOST — decomposed 2026-09-01 on Jonathan's three-part directive — TASK-744..755

_Archive note (2026-10-04): 4 terminal row(s) moved by `Tools/archive_board.py --rows` to `.claude/pipeline/archive/TASKBOARD-rows-056-MARKS-RECALL-GHOST-decomposed-2026-09-01-on-Jonathan-s-three.md` — TASK-753, TASK-754, TASK-757, TASK-768. Bytes unchanged; look them up there._

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim (three features, one message):** *"With the map that you pull up when walking up to the commander, I want you to be able to click on anywhere on the map, to create a circle on the map at that location. you can hover the mouse over it and use the mouse wheel scroll to make that circle larger or smaller. You can right click to delete that circle. Every time you make a new circle, it gets its own number in the middle of it. The first circle you create is circle "1", the next number you create is circle "2". The next number you create is circle "3", etc. This number system will also us to then communicate with the AI about where exactly we want units to be. For example, I can make 3 different circles and then tell the commander something like "move all units to hold 1" or "move all units to ambush 2", and the AI can use that indicated circle on the map to carry out the command. Also, I want to add a recall feature. From anywhere on the map, you can press "b", and that will allow the player to starting a recall animation similar to league of legends where after 10 seconds they teleport back to their castle and they completely refill their health. During this recall animation the player cannot attack and if they get hit with an attack it interupts the channel and they would have to press "b" again to start it from the beginning. I also want to add a respawn timer. If the player dies at any point during the match, they are dead for 3 minutes. During this time they instead get a ghost creature that they can control that is similar to their original body where it can command units, access the AI commander, and look at the map, it just cannot attack or be attacked. The enemy should be able to see this ghost as well. When the 3 minutes are up they respawn back at the castle."*

**Law was written FIRST (house rule)** — three NEW namespaces in CONVENTIONS.md. ⛔ **Every task below CITES them and ⛔ no task restates them:**

**RULING 1 — ⛔⛔ THE THREE FEATURES ARE ⛔ NOT THE SAME SIZE, AND THE BOARD SAYS SO OUT LOUD.**
**Feature 1 (map marks) = 3 tasks and it is the ⭐⭐ BIG ONE — ⛔ not because of the UI, but because a mark is a NEW REFERENT CLASS IN THE AI COMMAND GRAMMAR.** **Feature 2 (recall) = 2 tasks (one of them an art/asset carve).** **Feature 3 (respawn + ghost) = 2 tasks + 1 measurement — ⭐ and it is far SMALLER than it reads, because `SiegeGameMode` already ships the whole teleport-repossess-full-heal respawn and his 3 minutes is ONE NUMBER.** ⚖️ **Sizing them equally would have gold-plated the ghost and starved the referent.**

// ── SiegeMapMark.h (NEW — header-only pure data, the TeamId.h precedent) ──
struct FSiegeMapMark
{
    int32     Number   = 0;             // 1..MaxMapMarks. PERMANENT IDENTITY, never a list position (MARK-§ M-1).
    FVector2D WorldXY  = FVector2D::ZeroVector;   // arena world X/Y. NEVER printed into any prompt zone (MARK-§5 airlock).
    float     RadiusUU = 0.f;           // world-space radius the mark denotes.

    /** "circle_1". ⛔ NOT a bare digit — Zone A already ships `COUNT = 1 to 30` (MARK-§2).
     *  A pure static on purpose: the ONE seam the widget and the snapshot must agree on,
     *  and it is assertable by string equality with no world. */
    static FString MakeSymbol(int32 InNumber);
};

// ── SiegeMapMarkSubsystem.h (NEW) ──
UCLASS()
class GITCLAUDEUNREALTEST_API USiegeMapMarkSubsystem : public ULocalPlayerSubsystem
{
    GENERATED_BODY()
public:
    /** Adds at the LOWEST FREE number. Returns false (and mutates NOTHING) at MaxMapMarks. */
    bool AddMark(const FVector2D& WorldXY, float RadiusUU, FSiegeMapMark& OutMark);
    bool RemoveMark(int32 Number);                       // ⛔ LEAVES A HOLE. ⛔ NEVER renumbers (M-1).
    bool SetMarkRadius(int32 Number, float NewRadiusUU);
    const TArray<FSiegeMapMark>& GetMarks() const;
    void ClearMarks();                                   // match reset / PlayAgain (M-4)
};

### ⚖️ THE FIVE MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — ⛔⛔ THE VERDICT THAT SIZES EVERYTHING, AND IT WAS MEASURED, ⛔ NOT RELAYED.** A ladder is ⛔ **not** a geometry swap. **(a)** Recast cannot generate on a 76° face (the ceiling is 32.005°) ⇒ **a nav link is REQUIRED or the deck is an unreachable island**; **(b)** `ConstrainInputAcceleration` **deletes the vertical component of steering input for any walking or falling pawn, every frame, by design** (`CharacterMovementComponent.cpp:8121-8131`) ⇒ **custom movement is REQUIRED**; and **(c)** this project has **zero** nav links, **zero** `MOVE_Custom`, and exactly **one** `SetMovementMode` call in its entire source. ⇒ **This is greenfield traversal work.** Full table + line cites: **`TOWER-§8.1`**.

**RULING 2 — ⭐⭐ THE RIG IS NOW REQUIRED, AND THE MANAGER SAYS SO PLAINLY BECAUSE THE MANAGER IS WHO TOLD HIM OTHERWISE.** `TOWER-§1` deferred the climb clip on the honest ground that **a unit walking up a ramp looks fine unanimated**. **A ladder inverts that** — a unit gliding up a ladder bolt upright reads as broken. ⇒ **TASK-733 moves from *"polish, gated behind his sitting"* to **REQUIRED** and is **dispatchable NOW**; TASK-734 grows from *"drive them onto a walkable surface"* into real traversal work.** ✅ **The good news is unchanged and is repeated rather than buried: it is still ONE clip** — all three ranged units bind `SK_Footman_Skeleton` + `ABP_Footman`, and `RTG_MeshyBiped_to_SiegeBiped` ships.

**RULING 3 — ⭐ THE BATCH IS SEQUENCED SO THE TOWER IS ⛔ NEVER UNASCENDABLE ON `main`.** The re-authored mesh **deletes the ramp**; the traversal code **replaces it**. ⇒ ⛔ **They may NOT land in separate commits.** **ONE QA gate (TASK-741) · ONE compile + assemble + commit (TASK-742) lands the mesh, the clip, the ABP and both code diffs TOGETHER.** `main` goes *ramp-tower-playable* → *ladder-tower-playable* in a single step, with ⛔ **no intermediate state in which nobody can ascend.**

**RULING 4 — ⭐⭐ THE TWO LANES ARE GENUINELY PARALLEL, AND THE MECHANISM IS THE PINNED GEOMETRY + THE SOCKETS, ⛔ NOT OPTIMISM.** The obvious reading is that the code must wait for the mesh (it needs the ladder's coordinates). **It does not: `TOWER-§8.3` pins every coordinate as a BUILD TARGET for BOTH lanes** — the same move that pinned 2,078 uu before any mesh existed — **and `TOWER-§8.4`'s sockets let the code read the real geometry at runtime and fall back to the pinned literals with one warning.** ⇒ **the code is correct before the mesh lands and self-corrects when it does.** ⛔ **Neither lane blocks the other.**

**RULING 5 — ⛔ FILE OWNERSHIP IS DISJOINT AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE TWO *CODE* TASKS PARALLEL TOO.** **TASK-738 is the SOLE owner of `SummonedUnit.{h,cpp}`; TASK-734 is the SOLE owner of `ClimbableTower.{h,cpp}`.** ⚠️ **734 calls an API 738 declares, so 734 does not compile until 738 lands — ⭐ that is the DESIGNED state and it is a shipped precedent** (`MinerUnit.h:330-334`: *"Until that lands, these two overrides do not compile (C3668) — the designed state for this batch, which compiles as ONE UBT module"*). **The signature is pinned in `TOWER-§8.4` and ⛔ neither task may change it unilaterally.**

## HIGH-GROUND + WATCHTOWER — decomposed 2026-08-30 on Jonathan's four-ask directive — TASK-721..734

_Archive note (2026-10-04): 4 terminal row(s) moved by `Tools/archive_board.py --rows` to `.claude/pipeline/archive/TASKBOARD-rows-063-HIGH-GROUND-WATCHTOWER-decomposed-2026-08-30-on-Jonathan-s-f.md` — TASK-728, TASK-731, TASK-733, TASK-734. Bytes unchanged; look them up there._

**Jonathan's directive, verbatim:** *"notice with the map that the entire thing is black and turns to white with higher elevation locations, lets instead make it to where the entire map is green and goes from darker green to lighter green as elevation increases, try to make the green match as closely to the grass as possible. After that, lets give all archers and wizards and range units increased range. Triple the range of their attacks and make their attacks deal more damage the higher elevation they are. I would say that for every 5 feet that their elevation increases, their damage multiplier increases by 10%. Also, lets add a climable tower as a building card, make the cost 30 gold, and any ranged unit can climb it, so you will have to rig a climbing animation for all the ranged units."*

**Law was written FIRST (house rule)** — three surfaces in CONVENTIONS.md, ⛔ **every task below CITES them and ⛔ no task restates them:**
- **`WM-§8`** — an **AMENDMENT to the existing `WM-§2`**, ⛔ not a new namespace (a colour change to a shipped feature does not earn one). `§8a` what does not change · `§8b` the measured-grass law · `§8c` the legibility table · `§8d` the display/gameplay firewall.
- **`HIGH-§1..§8`** — NEW namespace. The pinned feet→uu arithmetic · the relative-to-target ruling · the one seam · the enumerated ranged set · the no-cap ruling with computed worst cases · the ×3 consequences.
- **`TOWER-§0..§6`** — NEW namespace. The one-rig measurement · the ship-first law · the ramp arithmetic · the card · the four behaviour rulings · the scope fences.

### ⚖️ THE SIX MANAGER RULINGS FOR THIS BATCH

**RULING 1 — ⛔⛔ THE FOUR ASKS ARE ⛔ NOT THE SAME SIZE, AND THE BOARD SAYS SO OUT LOUD.**
**Ask 1 (green ramp) = 2 tasks, and one of them is a MEASUREMENT.** **Ask 2 (×3 range) = 3 CSV cells inside a shared data task.** **Ask 3 (elevation damage) = 1 code task — and ⭐ it is the ask that delivers the most play value per line, because it works on the hills that are ALREADY in every match.** **Ask 4 (the tower) = 6 tasks + a gated follow-on chain.** ⚖️ **Sizing them equally would have starved the tower and gold-plated the ramp.**

**RULING 2 — ⛔⛔ `Docs/Data/cards.csv` HAS EXACTLY ONE OWNER (TASK-723), AND BOTH DATA ASKS LAND IN IT.**

    reliably, is a 20-second fallback a fallback — or is "full offload or the feature is off" the honest posture?** ⚠️ **Bar #4 says the model
    occupies 2.64 GiB of a 7.9 GB card (34 %), so full offload is available on the modal 8 GB machine** — the CPU path serves machines below
    that, and **it currently produces truncated, unusable orders on 2 of 5 attempts.**
    **(3) BAR #2's WORDING — I HAVE ALREADY RULED IT, AND THIS IS YOUR CHANCE TO OVERTURN ME.** The bar read *"TTFT + wall-clock … ≤ 2 s"* —
    one threshold, two quantities — and build-master rightly refused to resolve it in its own favour. **I ruled it a WALL-CLOCK bar
    (CONVENTIONS §12d): TTFT is not player-visible because the feature emits symbols only and has no streaming surface, so nothing reaches you
    until the whole order is parsed.** ⇒ **Under that reading bar #2 FAILS — partial 6472 ms vs ≤ 2000, cpu 8730 ms vs ≤ 6000 — and full offload
    measures 2106 ms.**
    ⚠️ **THE ONE NUMBER I WOULD PUT IN FRONT OF YOU: the BEST tier is 2.1 seconds — which is exactly the "2-second pause mid-battle" tolerance
    you named yourself at TASK-415.** The bar's text is mine; **the tolerance is yours**, and no measurement substitutes for it.
    **The standing context that makes a marginal call survivable:** the assistant is **strictly additive by law** (§2) — every key still works
    byte-identically and the console is never a requirement — but **default-follow means you now personally order every fight**, so an
    unreliable assistant makes the game worse rather than merely unhelpful.

## M7.7 tasks (decomposed 2026-07-23) — Deck-builder card details: click a card → "how it works" (TASK-268..272)

_Archive note (2026-10-04): 1 terminal row(s) moved by `Tools/archive_board.py --rows` to `.claude/pipeline/archive/TASKBOARD-rows-080-M7-7-tasks-decomposed-2026-07-23-Deck-builder-card-details-c.md` — TASK-268. Bytes unchanged; look them up there._

**Directive (verbatim, Jonathan, 2026-07-23):** *"lets change the deck builder interface a bit. Make it to where when you click on the display for a card it displays a detailed description on how the card works."*

**Manager rulings (binding for all five tasks; naming law in CONVENTIONS "Deck-builder card details — click-a-card 'how it works' (2026-07-23)", added FIRST):**

1. **Description SOURCE = GENERATED from DT_Cards (option b), not an authored CSV column (option a), not a hybrid (c).** Jonathan asked how the card *works* — mechanics, not flavor — and a **balance pass is explicitly pending** in the Standing backlog. Authored prose would go stale the day the numbers move, and it already HAS: the `Notes` column's `Lightning` row reads *"200 damage to the 3 highest-current-HP enemies in 400"* while that row's live `AoERadius` is **700**. Generated text re-derives from the row every frame, so a balance edit to cards.csv updates all 28 descriptions for free. Consequences: **no `Description` column, no `FCardRow` change, no DT_Cards reimport, and `Notes` is NEVER shown to the player** (it carries GDD refs + implementation identifiers). The only authored copy is a fixed keyword/type GLOSSARY in `DeckBuilderWidget.cpp` — ~15 strings covering keywords, not 28 cards — and mechanic magnitudes that are UPROPERTY defaults rather than CSV columns live there as named constants under the CONVENTIONS glossary-mirror rule.
2. **Add/remove does NOT move — there is no interaction conflict to resolve.** The orchestrator's finding assumed a whole-tile click adds a copy; the shipped tile does not have one. `WBP_DeckCardTile` binds `AddBtn`/`RemoveBtn` only (TASK-118 §element inventory), and TASK-125 made the card art `SelfHitTestInvisible` *specifically* so it never eats those clicks. So the card face is an UNBOUND gesture and details-on-click is purely ADDITIVE: `+`/`−`, the cap-grey, the x/50 counter, the average-cost guide and the exactly-50 `PlayBtn` gate are all untouched. (The new `Btn_CardFace` goes BOTTOM-most in the tile Overlay so the `+`/`−` plate keeps hit-test priority — this is the one thing that could regress M6, and it is an explicit acceptance item.)
3. **View form = NON-MODAL SIDE PANEL, inline in `WBP_DeckBuilder`.** Rejected: a modal (forces open/close per card, blocks `+`/`−`, and 28 cards means a lot of dismissing) and an expanded tile (re-flows the WrapBox and fights the runtime-constructed tree). A persistent right-hand panel lets Jonathan click card after card and compare while still editing the deck. **No new WidgetBlueprint asset** — and per the hard-won lesson, no new widget may ever be made by duplicate+REPARENT (silent RUNTIME-repaint corruption, ~9 wasted fixes); building inline sidesteps the class of defect entirely.
4. **LANE = branch `m7.6-arena10x`; INTEGRATION HELD until Jonathan's W1 look (TASK-219).** The feature's files (`DeckBuilderWidget.{h,cpp}`, `WBP_DeckBuilder`, `WBP_DeckCardTile`) have **zero** overlap with the branch's owned set (L_Arena.umap, DA_BattlefieldScatter, SiegePlayerController, SiegeBotController, CaptureZone), so there is no conflict either way — but the live working tree IS the branch and a checkout to main would swap L_Arena out from under an un-played W1 build. So: develop here, merge to main at the M7.6 Phase-6 gate. The HOLD is the conservative default, not a technical necessity: TASK-268 is file-only (no compile, no Git) and runs NOW; TASK-269..272 touch the editor/compiler/Git and would make the W1 build ≠ the `1e4bd19` build build-master verified — with a small but real risk of leaving `WBP_DeckBuilder` (a match-launch path) mid-surgery when he sits down to play. **FLAGGED: one word from Jonathan ("do it now") lifts the hold — the orchestrator should ask him at the next boundary rather than sit on it, since he is live.** **[CLEARED 2026-07-24: the W1 look is DONE — Jonathan APPROVED the W1 build (TASK-219). The hold is LIFTED; TASK-269 is dispatchable, TASK-270/271/272 follow in chain order (269 compile → 270 panel → 271 tile → 272 commit — order re-confirmed valid). The chain now develops on the live branch HEAD `0295f75`, not the earlier `1e4bd19`.]** **[LANE SHIFT 2026-07-25 — RESUME ON MAIN: M7.6 is now MERGED to main locally (merge `4c680bb`, not pushed); during that merge build-master parked the deck-builder trio UNCOMMITTED on main (milestone entry §7.6). So the chain RESUMES ON MAIN, not the branch — the branch-ownership rationale in this ruling is now MOOT (nothing to swap L_Arena out from under; the diff-guard simply confirms ONLY the three deck-builder files move). TASK-269..272 chain order + the TASK-270-271 completion recipe (handoffs/TASK-270-271.md) + the scaffolding already in the parked WBP are all STILL VALID for the resume. ⚠ COMPILE-VERIFY: TASK-268's `DeckBuilderWidget.{cpp,h}` were STASHED during the M7.6 merge compile, so the feature has NOT been built against M7.5+M7.6 together — TASK-269 must recompile + verify against MERGED main. Both editor-mutating tasks (this chain + TASK-297 SK-LODs) SERIALIZE on one exclusive editor session and run only when Jonathan is not in PIE. Commit backend + WBP together on main at TASK-272, no push.]**
5. **"Detailed description" scope (default chosen, non-blocking):** stat block **AND** keyword/rules explanations — i.e. what it costs, what its numbers are, and what every special rule on it actually does, in plain English with no GDD refs and no class names. **No flavor/lore text** this pass (Jonathan said "how the card works"). Adding a flavor line later = one authored CSV column and a 2-line composer change; it is deliberately not built now.
6. **Verification posture:** the description TEXT is machine-checkable (headless dump of all 28 strings, best-effort; QA reads them against cards.csv by hand). The RENDER and the CLICK are **not** — Slate screen-space UI is uncapturable headless and the deck builder needs a real menu click to open. Those close on Jonathan's eyes (recorded as a WATCH in TASK-272), per the CONVENTIONS pixel/human-check law. No "machine checks pass, ship it."

**FLAGGED for Jonathan (defaults chosen, nothing blocks):** (i) description = mechanics only, no flavor text — say the word for a flavor line; (ii) side panel, not a popup — a modal is a small rework if he prefers it; (iii) the panel is READ-ONLY (no `+`/`−` inside it) so the tile stays the single place a deck changes — a duplicate pair in the panel is easy to add later if he wants it; (iv) the hold in ruling 4; (v) the card TILES are still compact (TASK-125 flag: no fixed card size, sizing lives in the WrapBox slot) — the details panel now carries the big readable card face, which mostly answers that flag, but a proper tile-size pass is still open.

**Manager note (not a task, do not lose):** `CardRow.h`'s `ESpellDelivery` doc comment (lines ~70-76) says the `SpellDelivery` column header is "NOT yet appended to the CSV" — that is **STALE**: `Docs/Data/cards.csv` line 1 now ends with `SpellDelivery` and Fireball/FrostNova carry `HeroLine`. Comment-only correction; deliberately kept OUT of TASK-268's diff to keep QA's surface clean. Fold it into the next task that opens `CardRow.h`.

## W1 Unit-Commands tasks (decomposed 2026-07-23) — Shield Wall stances: ATTACK / HOLD / DEFEND (TASK-273..277)

_Archive note (2026-10-04): 3 terminal row(s) moved by `Tools/archive_board.py --rows` to `.claude/pipeline/archive/TASKBOARD-rows-081-W1-Unit-Commands-tasks-decomposed-2026-07-23-Shield-Wall-sta.md` — TASK-273, TASK-276, TASK-277. Bytes unchanged; look them up there._

**Directive (verbatim, Jonathan, 2026-07-23):** *"I want to implement a feature where you can press certain buttons to make the units around you do certain actions, similar to the video game 'shield wall'. For right now, I just want there to be 3 commands: 'hold' which makes all units move towards a specified location and only attack units within that specified location. 'defend' which makes all units head back towards the players castle and only attack units that are attacking the castle. 'attack' which makes all units attack the enemy castle and if there are any buildings or units that are within the spawn of the enemy castle they will prioritize those buildings or units before attacking the castle. This logic would only apply to the units with the 'Standard' targeting profiles... Lets put the 'attack' button on the 't' key, the 'hold' button on the 'r' key, and the 'defend' button on the 'e' key."*

**W1-SCOPED, NOT held.** Develops on `m7.6-arena10x` and INTEGRATES into the W1 build (unlike the M7.7 deck-details chain). Naming law in CONVENTIONS "Unit commands (Shield Wall stances) — ATTACK / HOLD / DEFEND (W1, 2026-07-23)", added FIRST. Applies ONLY to `ECardProfile::Standard` PLAYER (Blue) units; Siege/Support/None bodies + all bot units are UNTOUCHED.

**Manager rulings (binding for all five tasks):**
1. **Command STATE lives on `ASiegePlayerController`** (per-player, player-issued; the T/R/E bindings + ground reticle already live there; M8-ready). Not `ASiegeGameState` (would need per-team arrays; it is flagged local-only-through-M7).

### W1-PREP appendix 3a (2026-07-23) — BOT SPAWN ANCHOR CLAMP + ANTI-STACK (TASK-265..267; DEFECT, Jonathan: fix BEFORE the W1 look — TASK-267 is a DEFERRED robustness follow-up, explicitly NOT part of the W1 fix)

**Defect (found by build-master in the TASK-264 PIE capture-suite, `933fee4`):** bot units STACK on each other and FLOAT ~215–232 uu above ground at the Red spawn (two observed at identical XY 24192,−192). **Root cause (manager's reading, verified against the code — the programmer must still confirm before fixing):** TASK-262 shrank the bot spawn GATE to an 840 box around Castle_Red (X ≥ 24,160) but did NOT move the bot's spawn ANCHORS, which are still the pre-shrink geometry — rule-1 unit + rule-4 attack wave anchor at `CastleRed − BotCastleSpawnOffset(1750)` ⇒ X≈23,250, ~910 uu OUTSIDE the box. `ComputeValidBotSpawnPoint`'s ring-search maxes at 1,100 uu, so from X 23,250 the ONLY samples that clear the box edge are the +X-facing ones on the widest ring — every wave is served the same sliver at the boundary (exactly build-master's observed X 24,032–24,448 cluster) and piles up. The float is very likely the SYMPTOM (`AdjustIfPossibleButAlwaysSpawn` lifting capsules spawned inside each other), not an independent bug — CONFIRM, don't assume. **SECOND, UNREPORTED consequence of the same root cause (predicted, high confidence — verify in PIE):** rule-2a MINER and rule-2b DEEP MINE anchor at the target mine (thousands of uu from the box), so `ComputeValidBotSpawnPoint` FAILS every tick — and rule 2a `return`s on failure, so a bot holding an affordable Miner with a mine available STALLS its whole ordered-rules ladder (rules 3/4/5 never evaluated). The bot's economy is effectively dead on this branch. Expect a visibly different (better) bot at W1.

**Approach chosen — (a) spawn INSIDE the box and march out.** Rejected: (b) exempting bot march-waves from the box gate — it hands the bot a permanent 1,750-uu head start the player does not get and quietly re-opens the half-field spawn Jonathan just closed; (c) enlarging `SpawnBoxHalfExtent` — it enlarges the PLAYER box symmetrically (a balance change he'd have to accept) and does not fix stacking anyway. (a) is what the player already does (place in your box, units march), is the literal reading of Jonathan's directive, keeps M7.6 ruling #1 ("castle-front, then MARCH") intact — the anchor is still the centerline-facing front band of the castle box — and costs the wave ~1,750 uu of extra march ≈ 4 s at speed 400 on a 45,000-uu field. **Law added FIRST:** CONVENTIONS "W1-PREP additions 3" → anchor-clamp law + unit spawn clearance + spawn-Z law (appendix 3a).

**Load-bearing carve-out:** the clamp is a FALLBACK, not unconditional — an anchor that is ALREADY eligible (inside the box, or inside a Red-owned `CaptureZone_Center`) passes through untouched. That is what preserves TASK-264 PIE result (f) (the bot stages mid-field while Red holds the zone) — the emergent "spawn-forward" behavior Jonathan's directive explicitly asked for. An unconditional clamp would destroy it.

**RECONCILED 2026-07-23 (QA ACCEPTED TASK-265's flagged deviation — `qa/TASK-265.md`; the shipped behavior is now the law, CONVENTIONS appendix 3a updated to match):** the carve-out above proved NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. The pass-through alone can almost never fire for the zone, because no anchor in this class is normally *computed* inside the mid zone — so a box-only fallback would have deleted result (f) by construction (rule-2a's anchor is X-clamped to 0 by `IsOnOwnHalf`, and only from there does the 1,100-uu ring reach the ±840 zone; a box-only clamp moves it to X≈24,200, whence mid is unreachable) and left the bot half of the capture-zone feature dead code while the player keeps his. **Shipped law: an out-of-box anchor is clamped to the NEARER of the two ELIGIBLE regions — the Red castle box, or a Red-OWNED `CaptureZone_Center`.** QA verified it is INERT with no zone / a Neutral zone / a Blue-owned zone (byte-identical to the box-only spec) and that castle-relative anchors are always nearer the box (≈950 uu vs ≈22,450 uu) ⇒ M7.6 ruling #1 and rule-4 attack waves untouched; only rule-2 ECONOMY anchors can ever take the zone branch. Mid-staging is therefore now DETERMINISTIC rather than mine-Y luck — and an *attack* unit spawning at mid is a DEFECT to report, not this law.

### M5 — Spell system + Set III (TASK-097..109) — decomposed 2026-07-08

**Authorization:** Jonathan's 2026-07-08 directive ("After that, have the agents move on to M5") — pre-authorized while he is away, editor/MCP work included. Hard gate stands: if the editor MCP (127.0.0.1:8000) is unreachable, park the task and tell the orchestrator — never fake results. Naming law added to CONVENTIONS.md "Spells & Set III (M5)" BEFORE task issue.

**M5 manager decisions (binding for all M5 tasks):**
1. **Resolver home:** `USpellLibrary` (UBlueprintFunctionLibrary, SpellLibrary.h/.cpp) — the ONE spell-resolution path, shared by player controller (targeting mode) and bot. Pinned entry: `static bool ResolveSpell(UWorld* World, FName CardID, const FCardRow& Row, ETeamId CasterTeam, const FVector& TargetPoint)`. Effects dispatch on the `ESpellEffect` column.
2. **Data columns** per CONVENTIONS "Spells & Set III (M5)": SpellEffect / EffectDuration / MaxTargets / GoldSteal / ChainTargets / ChainFalloff; spells REUSE Damage + AoERadius. ECardType gains `Spell` if absent (TASK-097 flags the current enum shape + every downstream switch it touches).
3. **Spell castle scaling:** `USiegeDamageType_Spell` = 50% in `ACastle::TakeDamage` ONLY; buildings take FULL spell damage — Lightning (200) must kill an Arrow Tower (150 HP), it is the §4 "tower-killer". Mirrors the M2 Projectile precedent, NOT the M4 Siege both-rule. QA watch item.
4. **Lightning selection:** the MaxTargets highest **CURRENT-HP** enemy actors (units, hero, buildings/towers — **castle EXCLUDED**, anti-sniping intent) within AoERadius of the reticle; ties broken by distance to the reticle (deterministic). Flagged: current HP, not MaxHP (Slayer uses MaxHP — different concept).
5. **Freeze (FrostNova):** pinned API `ApplyFreeze(float Seconds)` on ASummonedUnit and ABuilding (+ `IsFrozen()`); freeze pauses movement/AI/attack cadence; refresh-not-stack (max of remaining vs new); castle never freezable; **hero NOT freezable in M5** (GDD §4 says "enemy units and towers" — flagged); **match-end FreezeAI has PRECEDENCE** — a spell-freeze expiry must never resume a match-end-frozen actor.
6. **Battle Cry (AllyBuff):** friendly units in AoERadius get +50% attack speed +25% move speed for EffectDuration (8 s); magnitudes = mechanic-rule UPROPERTYs (Rally precedent, GDD §4 comments). Self-refresh non-stacking; DOES stack with Rally and War Banner (independent systems) — QA watch.
7. **Pickpocket (GoldSteal):** resolves INSTANTLY on play — no reticle for a global effect (recorded deviation from §3.5; CardType stays Spell). Steal = min(GoldSteal, victim's gold), moved ONLY via existing ASiegePlayerState gold APIs (SetGold choke-point law; TASK-098 documents the exact API composition).
8. **Targeting mode (§3.5/§7):** reticle ANYWHERE on the map — no half restriction, no navmesh requirement; reticle TRACE-projected onto the surface under the cursor (**M4.5 terrain carry-in baked as LAW** — never assume the Z=0 plane); LMB confirm = deduct-then-resolve (card-leaves-hand-at-CONFIRM law; resolver false ⇒ full refund + HUD reason); RMB/Esc cancel free; reticle visual = decal w/ soft-referenced M_SpellReticle, null-safe. Cursor posture mirrors placement mode.
9. **Chain (Crystal Tower):** INSTANT-hit, no projectile actor. Primary = nearest valid enemy in Range (800); bounces to ChainTargets−1 more enemies, each within `ChainBounceRadius` = 350 (mechanic UPROPERTY — GDD unspecified, manager-defined) of the PREVIOUS target; damage Dmg − n×ChainFalloff (15/10/5); no friendly fire; no double-hit per zap; tagged USiegeDamageType_Projectile (tower attack family). Visual NS_ChainZap, null-safe.
10. **Bot spell rules** insert as rule 3 in the 2 s ordered loop (defend=1, miners=2, **SPELLS=3**, big unit=4, discard=5): 3a Fireball at ≥3 clustered player units (300-radius cluster); 3b Lightning at a player tower with ≥2 player units within 400. Affordability + card-in-hand checks as always; resolve directly through USpellLibrary (targeting mode is a human affordance); one LogSiegeBot line per fired rule (law). FrostNova/BattleCry/Pickpocket get NO bot cast rule (GDD is silent) — they fall through to rule-5 discard economics; flagged.

### M6 — Deck-builder meta (TASK-113..121) — decomposed 2026-07-09

**Authorization:** Jonathan's 2026-07-09 direct Claude Code M6 go-ahead ("move on to M6") after the M5.5 health-bar batch shipped. GDD mode: only M6 is decomposed. Naming law added to CONVENTIONS "Deck-builder & saved decks (M6)" BEFORE task issue; the two M5.5 process follow-ups are folded in (see "Follow-ups" below). Hard gates stand: editor/MCP work needs the editor MCP (127.0.0.1:8000) up — park + tell the orchestrator if unreachable (never fake results); nothing pushed. This batch does NOT touch M5's, M5.5's, or M4.5's state (all preserved on the board); M6 runs INDEPENDENT of parked M4.5.

**THE CRUX — build on the existing deck system, do not reinvent it (infra audited 2026-07-09):** `UDeckComponent::BuildAndShuffle()` (DeckComponent.h/.cpp) builds the draw pile from the `DeckCount` column of `/Game/Data/DT_Cards` and deals a 6-card hand; draw/discard/reshuffle/preview all exist and are frozen contracts. BOTH `ASiegePlayerController` (BeginPlay) and `ASiegeBotController` (OnPossess) own a `DeckComponent` subobject named `DeckComponent` and call `BuildAndShuffle()` at match start / `ResetDeck()` on Play Again — so TODAY every controller gets the SAME deck (the DeckCount column). `FCardRow` already carries `MaxCopies` (per-card cap) and `Cost` (average-cost math). M6 ADDS a per-controller override (a settable pending `FDeckList`) that `BuildAndShuffle` prefers when set-and-legal, else falls back to DeckCount — a purely additive seam, zero behavior change to the empty/unset path.

**M6 manager decisions (binding for all M6 tasks; each judgment call FLAGGED for QA + Jonathan):**
1. **Where saved decks live — FLAG 1 (RECOMMEND: SaveGame).** Player-authored named decks persist in a `USiegeDeckSaveGame` (`USaveGame` subclass) written to the fixed slot `"SiegeDecks"` (user index 0) → `Saved/SaveGames/SiegeDecks.sav`. Chosen over a DataAsset (NOT runtime-writable in a packaged build — can't save the player's edits) and a hand-rolled `.json` in `Saved/` (SaveGame is the idiomatic runtime-writable, cross-session, package-safe store). The SaveGame doubles as the menu→match handoff — the active deck is NOT passed through the level-open URL (50 CardIDs would bloat it; and the URL wouldn't persist across sessions anyway). Recommend SaveGame — ACCEPT unless Jonathan wants human-readable deck files.
2. **"Named decks" keyed by name — FLAG 2.** A deck is keyed by its `DeckName` (FString, player-entered). `SavedDecks` is a `TArray<FDeckList>`; `SaveDeckAs(Name)` overwrites a same-named entry (no silent duplicates); `ActiveDeckName` (FString) records which deck the next match uses. Reserved/empty name handling and a max-deck-count cap are left to the widget (flag any limit at TASK-118). Recommend name-keyed with overwrite-on-collision — ACCEPT.
3. **"Replace default deck with a legal curated one" — FLAG 3 (concrete meaning + M5-test-deck reconciliation).** The current `DeckCount` column is the M4/M5 TEST spread (22 cards spread to 50 so Set II/III were reachable pre-deck-builder — CONVENTIONS DeckCount registry note). TASK-115 RE-AUTHORS that column into a legal, intentional 50-card STARTER deck (a good curated deck, still `sum==50`, each `DeckCount<=MaxCopies`), superseding the test spread. This single cards.csv edit IS the "replace default deck" deliverable. The re-authored DeckCount is BOTH the deck-builder's "reset to default" template AND the match fallback when no legal saved active deck exists. cards.csv stays the single source of truth (§3.0). Recommend re-authoring DeckCount (not a parallel new asset) — ACCEPT; Jonathan may tweak the exact 50 at playtest (it's a CSV edit).
4. **Bot's "2 distinct decks" — definition + selection — FLAG 4.** `TArray<FDeckList> BotDecks` (EditDefaultsOnly) on `ASiegeBotController`, exactly TWO distinct legal curated decks as C++ constructor defaults (tunable per-BP; a deck composition is content, not a per-card stat → NOT a CSV column, mirroring the mechanic-rule-as-UPROPERTY precedent). At spawn the bot RANDOMLY picks one (`FMath::RandRange(0,1)`), logs it on `LogSiegeBot` (grep-able), and pushes it via `SetPendingDeckList`; missing/illegal entry ⇒ DeckCount fallback. Recommend random-of-2-at-spawn (variety across matches) over fixed/alternating — ACCEPT; Jonathan may prefer a fixed pairing at playtest.
5. **Copy-cap + exactly-50 enforcement — FLAG 5 (data-driven).** Both enforced from cards.csv: per-card `MaxCopies` caps `AddCopy` (the widget greys the "+" at the cap and refuses over-cap adds); the deck is legal (and "Play with this deck" enabled) ONLY at `TotalCount()==50`. The ONE legality function `UDeckLibrary::IsDeckLegal(CardTable, Deck, OutReason)` is shared by the widget, the DeckComponent build path, and the bot — no duplicated rules. Recommend the single shared data-driven validator — ACCEPT.
6. **Average-cost display (§8) — FLAG 6.** `UDeckLibrary::GetDeckAverageCost` = sum(Cost×Count)/TotalCount, shown as a soft guide (§8: <4 spams, >7 bricks; NO hard rule — it never blocks saving/playing). Data-driven from cards.csv Cost. Recommend display-only guide — ACCEPT.
7. **Tech reality — heavy UMG, editor-MCP-dependent — FLAG 7 (WATCH).** `WBP_DeckBuilder` is a heavy screen (28-card browser grid + per-card counters + x/50 + avg-cost + save/load list + play/back buttons). MCP CAN author full widget trees (PROVEN: TASK-041 built the complete interactive 6-slot hand; TASK-111 the health-bar widget) by duplicating a donor and rewiring incrementally — the working technique. It is EDITOR-MCP-dependent: if the MCP is down, TASK-118 parks and tells the orchestrator. The C++ base (`UDeckBuilderWidget`) owns ALL model/logic so the WBP is layout + BlueprintCallable calls + float/int/bool/FString BIEs (never enum/struct BP params — widget rule). The main-menu already has a greyed Deck Builder button (TASK-049) — the screen wires to it (`Btn_DeckBuilder`, enable + open as a viewport overlay on L_MainMenu; no new level/game mode).
8. **Verification reality — FLAG 8 (WATCH + the follow-up that fixes it).** Save/load and the exactly-50 gate are largely MACHINE-verifiable (SaveGame readback + DeckComponent deck-content readback in PIE — no human input needed). The LIVE click-through of the 28-card grid (add/remove feel, greyed caps, the counters updating) is a human WATCH on Jonathan's unlocked desktop (locked-desktop = no SendInput, TASK-076/112 doctrine). TASK-121 (the debug-exec cheat, follow-up 2) is issued IN this milestone so build-master can drive combat-side verification (health bars, castle HP, spawns) headlessly starting with M6's own TASK-120 — it does not help the grid click-through, which stays a human WATCH.

**Follow-ups from the M5.5 build (how handled):**
- **(1) CONVENTIONS include-rule** — handled as a CONVENTIONS coding-law note ("Complete-type include law", C++ section), NOT a task: a `.cpp` upcasting/dereferencing a forward-declared component (e.g. `GetCapsuleComponent()`) must `#include` that type's header; QA now scans every code task for it. This is what broke TASK-110's first compile.

Placed in M6 because the follow-up notes it "would pay off starting with M6's own verification."

**M6 exit criteria (playable slice):** from the main menu, the (now-enabled) Deck Builder button opens `WBP_DeckBuilder`; the screen browses all 28 cards, adds/removes copies with each card's `MaxCopies` enforced (the "+" refuses/greys at the cap), shows a live "x/50" counter and an average-cost readout (§8); "Play with this deck" is enabled only at exactly 50; the player saves and loads NAMED decks that survive quitting and relaunching the game (SaveGame); the active saved deck FEEDS the next match (the player's in-match hand is dealt from it, verified by DeckComponent readback) and, with no legal saved deck, the match falls back to the curated 50-card DeckCount default; the bot plays with one of its 2 distinct curated decks (random pick logged on LogSiegeBot). Recordable: UI/UX + save-load systems clip.
